options.systemMessage:
You are a client brief analyst. Extract key context from unstructured client briefs.

Your task:
1. Read the provided client brief document (unstructured format)
2. Extract key information about:
   - Brand voice and tone
   - Target audience demographics and psychographics
   - Content themes and topics of interest
   - Brand values and messaging pillars
   - Competitive positioning
   - Content restrictions or guidelines
   - Campaign objectives or goals

IMPORTANT:
- Handle varying brief structures - no predetermined sections
- Extract what is available, mark missing information as null
- Summarize key points concisely
- Focus on actionable context for content recommendations

Return valid JSON only.

parameters.text:
=HOW TO WRITE THIS REPORT

The page that renders your words already shows the numbers: six KPI tiles with their month-over-month deltas, a card per platform, the top posts with their own figures, the pillar chart. Write beside that, not over it.

- Never spend a sentence restating a figure the page already shows. Use a number only when it is the point of the sentence, and at most two figures in one sentence.
- Write every insight, takeaway and opportunity as a claim of at most 12 words, then a colon, then the evidence in one sentence. Example: "Channel mix is the clearest gap: YouTube took 8 of 24 posts while Reels drove most of the engagement." The report splits on that colon to make a headline, so the claim must stand alone.
- One claim per field. No preamble, no "the data shows", no repeating the client name in every sentence.
- Name a company by its brand name. Where you only have a website, write it as a brand ("reyeslaw.com" becomes "Reyes Law"). Never put a URL in prose.
- Every recommendation is something the team can start this week: it names the platform, the format, how often, and what to measure.

LENGTH, in characters, and these are limits rather than targets:
- month_over_month_summary: two sentences, 260 in total, leading with the biggest move.
- key_insights: 3-5 items, 180 each, in the claim-colon-evidence shape.
- top_performing_content: 90 each. pillar_alignment.recommendations: 160 each, each an instruction with a format and a cadence.
- platform_breakdown: headline 90, insights 150 each, three at most.
- trends analyses: overview 220; top_themes 60 each; successful_formats 70 each; opportunities_for_client 160 each, each naming the format, the cadence and what to measure; key_takeaways 140 each.
- competitive_takeaways, when the competitive context is present: 200 each.

---

{{ $json.competitive_context ? ('COMPETITIVE CONTEXT (from the latest competitor analysis of ' + ($json.competitive_context.landscape || 'the RivalIQ landscape') + ', analyzed ' + ($json.competitive_context.analyzed_at || '') + '):\n' + JSON.stringify($json.competitive_context) + '\n\nUSE IT: (1) In sprout_performance_analysis.key_insights, compare the client against the competitive set where the data supports it (cadence, engagement rate, channel mix, share of voice). (2) pillar_alignment.recommendations and the trend opportunities MUST respond to the competitive picture: the empty posting windows, the winner patterns (in the client\'s own voice), and the hashtag, format and copy-angle gaps. (3) endorsed_gaps (if present) were approved by the account team: treat each as a requirement the recommendations must visibly answer at least once, and name it there. suppressed_gaps (if present) were rejected by the team: never propose them or anything equivalent. (4) Add a top-level array "competitive_takeaways" with 3-5 short, specific sentences (each citing a number or a named competitor) describing how this report responds to the competitive picture, including which endorsed gaps it answers. Do not invent competitor data beyond what is provided.\n\n---\n\n') : '' }}{{ JSON.stringify($json) }}

{{ (Array.isArray($json.sprout?.profiles) && $json.sprout.profiles.length) ? '' : 'NO CONNECTED PERFORMANCE DATA. This brand has no Sprout Social profile connected yet, so there are no KPI tiles, platform cards or top posts behind this report. Do not invent, estimate or imply any performance figure. In month_over_month_summary and key_insights say in one sentence that performance analysis starts once the brand\'s social accounts are connected, leave top_performing_content empty, and base pillar_alignment on the brief and the content pillars only. Put the weight of the report on the trend analysis and the competitive context when present.' }}

assignments.name: previous_month_start
assignments.value: ={{ (() => { const s = $json.body?.date_range_start || $json.date_range_start; const e = $json.body?.date_range_end || $json.date_range_end; if (s && e) { const a = DateTime.fromISO(s); const b = DateTime.fromISO(e); const days = Math.max(1, Math.round(b.diff(a, 'days').days) + 1); return a.minus({ days }).toFormat('yyyy-MM-dd'); } return $now.minus({ months: 1 }).startOf('month').toFormat('yyyy-MM-dd'); })() }}

assignments.name: previous_month_end
assignments.value: ={{ (() => { const s = $json.body?.date_range_start || $json.date_range_start; const e = $json.body?.date_range_end || $json.date_range_end; if (s && e) { return DateTime.fromISO(s).minus({ days: 1 }).toFormat('yyyy-MM-dd'); } return $now.minus({ months: 1 }).endOf('month').toFormat('yyyy-MM-dd'); })() }}

nodes.notes: trigger-scheduled-reports sends stagger_seconds (0, 180, 360, ...) per client on the monthly run day so the nine social pipelines start three minutes apart instead of all at once (Apify actor memory, Sprout and Gamma quotas). Runs from the app carry no stagger and continue immediately.
